mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25 percentage points for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% in the same month indicates a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with disinflation, which can create uncertainty and risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 12-month moving average by >10% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2% in the same month indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >0.5% and UNRATE falls >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered months at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals a prolonged economic stagnation, which erodes corporate earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annualized growth < 1% for four consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance.
